source_name: CBCG blog — 'Pregled FinTech ekosistema u Crnoj Gori' (fintech ecosystem mapping)
why_relevant: Regulator's own mapping exercise covering banks, MFIs, payment institutions and e-money institutions — a ready-made actor inventory and terminology source for the payments landscape, published by the body that licenses it.

source_name: CBCG — Strateški plan 2025–2028 (Strategic Plan)
why_relevant: CBCG's own multi-year strategy naming the payment-system, SEPA-alignment, cash-operations and IT modernisation objectives that generate procurement. Best available forward-looking proxy for a procurement pipeline given that no public procurement plan page was found.

source_name: Pravilnik o načinu sprovođenja jednostavnih nabavki (simple-procurement rulebook, UJN)
why_relevant: Defines the below-threshold regime (goods/services up to EUR 15,000, works up to EUR 30,000) handled outside full CeJN procedures and reported only in semi-annual reports (1 Jan-30 Jun, 1 Jul-31 Dec). Directly explains a structural blind spot for small POS/terminal/maintenance orders and points to where those purchases can still be recovered.

source_name: Consolidated text of the Zakon o javnim nabavkama (Sl. list CG 074/19, 003/23, 011/23) - PDF on ujn.gov.me
why_relevant: The operative statute itself: defines contracting authorities, thresholds triggering publication, procedure types, and the mandate for the electronic procurement system. Baseline document against which every future amendment (committed for Q2 2026) must be diffed.

source_name: DRI — IT / information-system audits (revizija informacionih sistema)
why_relevant: DRI runs a dedicated IT-audit line (2 IT audits in a recent year alongside 25 regularity and 6 performance audits). These reports describe the procured systems, the vendors, IT security/continuity gaps and the contracting history — the closest thing in Montenegro to an independent assessment of state IT/payment-adjacent system procurement.

source_name: DRI — Godišnji izvještaj o izvršenim revizijama i aktivnostima (annual audit activity report)
why_relevant: Annual consolidated report giving the year's audit programme, systemic procurement findings and recommendation follow-up. Best single document for tracking which entities are under audit scrutiny and which procurement failure modes recur.

source_name: Montenegrin business press coverage of procurement appeals (e.g. Standard.co.me)
why_relevant: Domestic media report individual appeal outcomes with named bidders, disputed amounts and the intention to escalate to the Administrative Court — a low-latency signal that a contested award exists, often before the decision PDF is indexed.

source_name: MANS — National Integrity System assessment (NIS, Transparency International methodology)
why_relevant: Institution-by-institution assessment of Montenegro's oversight bodies (anti-corruption agency, DRI, independent bodies, SOEs) using TI methodology. Gives a calibrated view of which oversight sources are actually credible and enforceable — useful metadata for weighting every other source in this cell.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA (TIPS Clone) project documents
why_relevant: Project Appraisal Document (Report No. PADHI01235) for the flagship Montenegro payments project; contains the procurement plan summary, components, implementing agency (Central Bank of Montenegro / Ministry of Finance) and indicative contract packages for the TIPS-clone instant-payment build. Directly names what will be tendered.

entity_name: EUME / Kancelarija za evropske integracije Crne Gore
source_name: eu.me — Montenegro EU-integration portal, procurement alignment reporting
why_relevant: Official EU-integration communication describing CEJN's scope in authoritative terms — that all public calls, plans, decisions, complaints and contract implementation must be available through CEJN, with user counts. Best single citation for what the outcome-side register is legally supposed to contain, and a pointer to Chapter 5 (public procurement) accession documentation.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Enlargement Report (Chapter 5: Public Procurement)
why_relevant: Annual EU assessment with a dedicated public-procurement chapter covering the remedies system, transparency of intergovernmental-agreement procurement, and reform trajectory. Sets the reform agenda that will shape future tender rules — including e-procurement and IT spending.

source_name: MAPS — Assessment of Montenegro Public Procurement System 2024
why_relevant: Full methodological assessment of the Montenegrin procurement system, including remedies/appeals pillar and market-level spend analytics. The single densest English-language reference on how the system works, its data availability and its weaknesses.

source_name: MAPS e-procurement assessment of Montenegro's public procurement system (2024)
why_relevant: Independent 2024 assessment documenting how the CeJN e-procurement system publishes data, what is machine-readable, registration volumes and gaps. It is the authoritative reference for judging what any aggregator can actually harvest from ME and where aggregators must fill holes — essential input to the access-review of every paid platform in this cell.

source_name: SIGMA (OECD/EU) — Public Administration in Montenegro monitoring reports
why_relevant: SIGMA scores Montenegro's public procurement and remedies system against EU principles, including explicit assessment of the review body's capacity, timeliness and decision quality — an external calibration of how much weight to place on Commission data.

source_name: Belit d.o.o. - vendor of the CeJN platform (product page)
why_relevant: The company that built CeJN for the Montenegrin Ministry of Finance under an EC/IPA-funded project. Vendor documentation describes the system's modules and data model (planning, notices, decisions, complaints, contracts, execution reports), which is the fastest way to understand what data fields and endpoints a collector can expect from CeJN.

source_name: Borba.me and Dan.co.me — investigative reporting on CBCG procurement specifications
why_relevant: Montenegrin outlets that scrutinise CBCG's procurement plan line items and tender technical specifications (e.g. reporting that a vehicle tender's specifications appeared to be written around a single model). Valuable both as evidence that a CBCG plan javnih nabavki exists and circulates, and as a signal of specification-steering — relevant when assessing whether a CBCG payments or cash-handling tender is genuinely contestable.

source_name: Businesswire / vendor newswire distribution (e.g. Ripple–CBCG agreement)
why_relevant: Concrete precedent that supplier-issued newswire releases are the public record of Montenegrin financial-sector engagements: Ripple announced its CBDC strategy/pilot agreement with the Central Bank of Montenegro via Businesswire. Newswire archives are searchable for 'Montenegro' + vendor names.

entity_name: CMS Expert Guide to public procurement
source_name: CMS Expert Guide to public procurement - Montenegro chapter
why_relevant: Law-firm practice commentary structured around exactly the variables this cell tracks: where notices must be published, value thresholds (states EUR 25,000 supplies/services, EUR 30,000 works), procedure types, appeal deadlines and fees, and whether e-procurement is mandatory. Authored by CMS lawyers with Podgorica/Belgrade coverage. NOTE: the version read appears partly out of date (refers to a 'State Commission for Control of Public Procurements' and voluntary e-procurement), so treat its figures as needing verification against the 2019/2023 law - which is itself a useful signal of how fast law-firm content ages.

source_name: CRNVO - NGO-hosted archive of the Law on Public Procurement
why_relevant: NGO resource centre mirror of the promulgated law text; useful as a redundancy copy of historical versions when official pages are reorganised (a recurring problem with gov.me migrations).

source_name: European Payments Council — Montenegro SEPA accession coverage
why_relevant: Authoritative account of Montenegro's SEPA entry and the sector-wide go-live schedule. SEPA and TIPS-clone migration is the single largest forcing function for PSP and bank technology procurement in this market, so it dates the demand wave this cell tracks.

source_name: monte.business — Montenegro Business (English news site)
why_relevant: Reported Montenegro signing an agreement for a real-time instant payment system with Italy's central bank — a concrete cross-border technology/service arrangement of exactly the kind rarely visible in national notice portals. Note this domain is distinct from montenegrobusiness.eu despite similar branding; treat provenance carefully.

source_name: OECD/SIGMA - Central public procurement institutions in the Western Balkans
why_relevant: Directly addresses central purchasing bodies - the structural change most likely to concentrate future payments-hardware and IT procurement into a few large framework agreements, changing where and how such tenders appear.

source_name: OTP banka d.d. (Croatia) — group expansion news on Montenegro
why_relevant: Illustrates the pattern this cell exists to capture: a Montenegro-relevant corporate/structural announcement published by a sister/parent entity in another country, in Croatian, not by the Montenegrin bank. Sister-bank newsrooms (HR, RS, SI) are an under-watched channel for ME-affecting group decisions.

source_name: Paragraf.me - Zakon o javnim nabavkama Crne Gore (consolidated law)
why_relevant: Consolidated text of the Montenegrin Public Procurement Act with amendments. Defines which entities are obliged contracting authorities (explicitly including the Central Bank), thresholds, procedure types, the 'jednostavne nabavke' simple-procurement regime and mandatory publication duties - i.e. the rules that determine what is and is not visible on CeJN.

source_name: Sandžak Press — regional Balkan news portal covering Montenegro procurement disputes
why_relevant: Concrete worked example of the exact story type this cell targets: a partially annulled tender for ANPR/OCR equipment and software after a rights-protection complaint alleging tailored, competition-limiting documentation. Demonstrates that regional portals republish Montenegrin procurement-dispute reporting and are therefore a usable redundancy channel when the originating outlet is paywalled or offline.
